solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fair punishment, as only sweets mentioned

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: only means just, and sweets are desserts, giving a phrase that is said the same way as the answer

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a fair punishment would involve nothing but pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for getting what one deserves, typically a fitting penalty for bad behaviour.

clue.text: Short cheerful pleasure trip

indicators.note: short tells us to cut the last letter off the word for cheerful

parts.note: jaunty means cheerful and lively

explanation.surface: A brief, happy little outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like part of the definition, but it trims the final Y from JAUNTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a short excursion taken for fun.

clue.text: Call for help about care in bad circumstances

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the distress call goes round the other letters

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of care in are in poor order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone appeals for assistance with poor care in difficult conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges CARE IN; 'about' wraps the distress call round those letters, splitting it as S and OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: possible situations or sets of events that might unfold.

clue.text: A particular detachment of troops

definitions.meaning: a single item or point, as in 'every last particular'
a small group of soldiers assigned to a special duty

explanation.surface: A specific small unit of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one small item or fact, and a squad sent off on a particular task.

clue.text: Like this parking concession

parts.note: so means in this way
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A parking allowance described as being of this sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something small given to appease or placate someone.

clue.text: Rice dish in foremost of restaurants — it's too exotic

indicators.note: foremost of picks the leading letter of restaurants
exotic suggests something strange and unusual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A food critic remarks that a rice dish at leading restaurants is too foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' turns IT'S TOO into ISOTTO, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Activity at St Moritz? Last of passengers currently embarking

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of passengers

parts.note: now means at the present time
boarding means getting on a ship, plane or train

explanation.surface: Travellers getting on board at a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: St Moritz is a Swiss ski resort, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a winter sport done on the slopes of an Alpine resort.

clue.text: Singer in bar, one over in centre of Montreux

parts.note: a counter is the bar in a pub or shop

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the reversed number goes within the middle letters
centre of picks the two middle letters of Montreux
over means turned over, so the word one reads backwards

explanation.surface: A singer is in a bar somewhere in the middle of a Swiss lakeside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' gives ENO, which goes 'in' TR, the centre of Montreux.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a male singer whose voice reaches the alto range.

clue.text: Work with uranium, fast becoming rich

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone works with uranium and gets wealthy quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun, a period of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: luxurious and lavish, showing wealth.

clue.text: Taken from recipes, tomato sauce

indicators.note: taken from means the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tomato sauce copied out of a recipe book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tomato sauce' looks like the definition; only 'sauce' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an Italian basil and pine-nut sauce.

clue.text: A linen hat ordered for boy

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A linen hat was bought for a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'bought' but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a male first name, so a boy's name.

clue.text: Runaway victory of country team rounding lake

parts.note: land means a country

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so the team word surrounds the letter for lake

parts.note: a side is a sports team
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A national team wins handsomely around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an overwhelming election or contest win, like ground collapsing all at once.

clue.text: Bill in club, withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word for club reads backwards

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A bill at a club has been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a members' club, but it is the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a running bill at a bar or restaurant.

clue.text: I grew agitated holding a small insect

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the scrambled letters hold the single letter
agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone became upset at having a little bug in their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns I GREW into EWRIG, which holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small insect with pincers at the tail end.

clue.text: Wine, mostly red — sat in getting drunk

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the colour

parts.note: taken as the colour word, which loses its final letter

indicators.note: getting drunk suggests the letters are reeling and out of order

explanation.surface: Someone sat inside drinking mostly red wine and became tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts RED to RE; 'getting drunk' turns SAT IN into TSINA.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Yarn from an artist about travel

indicators.note: about here means next to or after, placing the artist's letters following the word for travel

parts.note: go means to travel
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A tale told by a painter about a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a story but is wool.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: soft wool spun from the hair of a rabbit or goat.

clue.text: Reportedly fixed old plasterwork

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the words are matched by their spoken form

parts.note: fixed means stuck, and old is the abbreviation O, together said like the answer

explanation.surface: Old plaster has, it is said, been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: fine plaster used to coat walls or make mouldings.

clue.text: Briefly carry toddler

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for carry loses its last letter

parts.note: tote means carry

explanation.surface: A parent picks up a small child for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a very young child.

clue.text: Fulfilled? Sure

explanation.surface: A question about being content followed by a confident answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: content with what one has, and convinced that something is true.

clue.text: Gather inside train ferry

indicators.note: inside means the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Collect people inside a train ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' suggests collecting; here it means deduce.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to conclude something from evidence.

clue.text: Sound of hooter I installed

indicators.note: installed means put in place within, so the letter goes inside the word for hooter

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose

explanation.surface: A car horn I fitted makes a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' suggests a horn but is slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: The French put up close to Canterbury, a cathedral city

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards, so the article reads backwards

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: close to picks the final letter of Canterbury

explanation.surface: French visitors staying near Canterbury in another cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small city in Cambridgeshire, England, famous for its cathedral.

clue.text: Female cutting inch of woven fabric

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the letter for female goes inside
woven means interlaced, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman trims an inch off some woven cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' turns INCH OF into CHIFON, which F cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a sheer, lightweight cloth of silk or nylon.

clue.text: Cash column includes article that's off-the-peg

parts.note: ready, or readies, is British slang for cash

indicators.note: includes means contains, so the column word surrounds the article

parts.note: a tower is a tall column
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A financial column featuring a piece on off-the-shelf clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' suggests a newspaper column; it is a tall structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: clothes made in standard sizes, not tailored to order.
